title: A cut pushes the release to every remote, and the public repository takes the workroom's name: push the workroom to local only and publish the snapshot through CI (ST0010)
body:
A cut pushes the release commit and its tag to every remote in release.remotes. devbin declares none, so a cut pushes to every remote: canon's local, and its upstream, matthewsinclair/devbin. ST0010 recreates that name as the PUBLIC repository (decision 56), and the workroom then keeps no GitHub copy (decision 56 (2)). Left as it is, the first cut after the recreate would push the private workroom (intent/ and the whole history) into the public repository.

The cut's pre-flight also refuses unless CI is green on the pushed commit (decision 62, issue 0223), and that read is of the workroom's GitHub copy, which is gone after the recreate.

hv approved ST0010's plan on 2026-10-27 (vc decision 78): safety comes first. CI runs on the snapshot commit, pushed to a candidate branch of the public repository, and main and the tag follow once it is green (Q3 (a)).

## Measured

On main at 4ccfde65:
- lib/cmd/release pushes once per remote in its push plan (1120-1150). The plan is built from `cfg_release_list remotes` (546, 2070), which is every remote when the key is absent.
- bin/.devbin/config.yaml declares no release.remotes.
- Canon's remotes are local, a Dropbox bare repository with no remotes of its own, and upstream, matthewsinclair/devbin over ssh.
- packaging/homebrew/devbin.rb's url is ssh://git@github.com/matthewsinclair/devbin.git, and its comment says it becomes https once the repository is public.

## Design

cc's design, approved by vc on 2026-10-27 with R1, is ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/publish/design-0239-0240.md (sha256 43bad350). vc's review is ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/reviews/design-0239-0240.review.md (sha256 570141bf).

- **The cut.** A publishing project declares release.publish.url. Its cut runs through push, to release.remotes alone (devbin's is local), and then stops, with its snapshot, candidate and publish rows pending.
- **`release publish <vX.Y.Z> [--expect <sha>] [--dry-run] [--yes]`** runs these steps:
  - **resolve.**
  - **pre-flight:** the url answers; the public refs are read; no workroom remote names the publish repository (R1); the list reads; ci.query is declared. A remote names the publish repository when its url or pushurl matches it by OWNER/NAME on any host, through url_host_path, so an ssh host alias counts.
  - **snapshot:** 0239's builder, on the public tip. `--expect` refuses any other sha.
  - **confirm.**
  - **candidate:** a push to `candidate/{tag}`, never forced, then ci.query on the snapshot's sha, bounded by ci.wait.
  - **publish:** the publish branch fast-forwarded, and a lightweight tag at the snapshot, each read back. A tag that already exists elsewhere is refused.
  - **object, after and ci:** as today, against the public repository.
- **CI.** Under publish.url, ci.base is refused, and its guarantee moves to the candidate step. tests.yml's push filter gains candidate/**, and a candidate push runs the tag's whole matrix, macOS and WSL included (decision 81).
- **The formula.** Its revision is the public tag's commit, read by ls-remote. The template's url becomes https, in the release whose snapshot first reaches the public repository.
- **A project without publish.url** cuts exactly as today.

## Done when

1. With release.remotes naming local, a dry-run cut's push plan names local alone. A publishing project's cut stops after push, with its snapshot, candidate and publish rows pending, and a stand-in public remote receives nothing from it.
2. `release publish` pushes the snapshot, never a workroom commit, to `candidate/<tag>`. It moves the publish branch and pushes the tag only after ci.query reads green on the snapshot's sha. On red, on a run still going past ci.wait, or on an unreadable read, it moves neither and says why. `--expect` refuses any other sha. The arms use a stub ci.query, as releasecut.bats's do.
3. The pre-flight refuses, naming the remote, when any workroom remote's url or pushurl names the publish repository by OWNER/NAME on any host, an ssh host alias included (R1). An arm holds each form.
4. Every public ref is read back at the snapshot, no push forces, and a public tag already at another commit is refused.
5. Under publish.url, validation refuses ci.base, tests.yml runs on candidate/** pushes with the tag's whole matrix, macOS and WSL included (decision 81), and the formula's revision is the public tag's commit, with an https url. A project without publish.url cuts exactly as today.
6. lib/pages/release.md and the config reference document the verb and its keys. The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU with the tree scans and help, and CI is green on the pushed head.

## Resolution

Fixed at e105491adead0dd247289d1897b59de8d413d43e, landed on main by vc with the rest of C (fb66b479..7565e2a2) on hv's GO of 29 Oct, as cc banked it. A project that declares release.publish.url cuts to release.remotes alone and stops after its push, and `release publish <vX.Y.Z> [--expect <sha>] [--dry-run] [--yes]` makes the tag's snapshot public through CI on that very commit: candidate/{tag} first, the publish branch and a lightweight tag only once ci.query reads it green, nothing ever forced.

- **The cut under publish.url.** Push goes to release.remotes as before. A remote it pushes to that names the publish repository is refused at pre-flight, through `release_remote_naming` (lib/release.steps), which now takes the remotes to ask, and so is one whose url says too little to tell. _RELEASE_STEP_NAMES gains snapshot, candidate and publish after push; a publishing cut stops there at exit 0, those three rows pending on release publish, and object, after and ci `not reached`, a new row state. Without publish.url the three read `skipped`, and the cut runs as before. release status prints the same rows, `not read` under publish.url, another new state, since it reads no public repository, and its confirm row no longer counts a release object release publish makes.
- **What names the publish repository** (vc's C1 and W1). `_release_repo_key` reads a url's OWNER/NAME, and reads it again past the leading slashes of its path where url_host_path finds none, so `git@github.com:/t/pub.git` and `https://github.com//t/pub.git` name t/pub. A local path is compared by what it resolves to, `-ef`, or as written where either is not there. `release_remote_naming` answers rc 2, naming why, when the remotes cannot be listed or when publish.url or a remote's url names a host and no OWNER/NAME that can be read, and each of its three callers refuses on rc 2 rather than read it as another repository: the publishing cut's pre-flight, release publish's pre-flight and the snapshot builder before it fetches a parent.
- **release publish,** a verb of release.verbs, behind a gate as a cut is: resolve; a pre-flight naming every refusal and writing nothing (R1 over every remote's url and pushurl, the url never read when one names it; the tag's commit carries the release and the list; ci.query declared; release.repo declared where the object needs gh; the public branch, candidate and tag read); the snapshot, through snapshot_build in the run's scratch, `--expect` taking the whole sha and refusing any other, and a public tag or candidate holding another commit refused before any push; confirm; the candidate, pushed and read back, then ci.query asked about the snapshot's sha with no tag, up to ci.wait, only green going on; publish, main fast-forwarded and the tag pushed lightweight, each read back, then the candidate deleted and its absence read back. The deletion carries an explicit lease, `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<candidate>:<snapshot>`, so it happens only while the candidate still holds the snapshot and forces nothing (R4). Then a cut's object, after and ci, against the public repository. Every call to it is made from a repository of the run's own (_snapshot_remote), and every push is bounded (cut_call).
- **Published means both** (vc's W2): the publish branch and the tag both at the snapshot. A tag there by another hand, with the branch still to move, waits on CI on the candidate as any publish does. An older version run again after a later one is public is refused as public already, its tag in the branch's history.
- **One code path for both verbs:** the cut's confirm-step object read (cut_object_left), its question (cut_confirm), its object, after and ci steps and its end (cut_tail), and a dry run's verdict (cut_dry_verdict) are lifted out of cut_run unchanged, and release publish calls them. The notes-body calls name their steps, confirm and tag, where they passed 6 and 7.
- **A published snapshot is found, never made twice:** where the publish branch's tip is itself the snapshot of the commit, snapshot_build makes that commit on the tip's own parent in the scratch, finds the tip, and takes it, so a publish stopped after main moved, or run again once finished, reads the same sha. Its commits are made by one function, _snapshot_commit_tree.
- **Config:** release.publish.candidate (default candidate/{tag}, holding {tag} and more, read only beside publish.url); ci.base refused under publish.url; ci.query with ci.tag and ci.base off accepted under publish.url, where the candidate asks it; publish among release.verbs, and in the readers of every key it reads; and a project that declares publish.url and leaves publish out of a declared release.verbs is refused by validation, since its cut would stop after the push and nothing would make the release public.
- **CI:** tests.yml runs on pushes to candidate/**, and the macOS and WSL jobs and Test Summary's requirement run on a candidate as on a tag (decision 81).
- **The formula:** under publish.url its revision is the public tag's commit, read by ls-remote through release_git_remote, and a release not public yet is refused. One reader, release_listed_tag, reads a public tag and its peel for the formula and release publish, and one, snapshot_publish_branch, reads the publish branch for the snapshot and release publish. The template's url is https.
- **devbin's config:** release.remotes [local], publish.url https://github.com/matthewsinclair/devbin.git, ci.base removed, ci.tag off, and ci.wait 90m, since a candidate runs the whole matrix.

Documented in lib/pages/release.md, docs/configuration.md, lib/config.reference.yaml and docs/releasing.md. ci_query_decl moves into the release fixtures, and state_of reads a two-word state whole.

Two residuals vc accepted. The candidate branch reading back at a different commit at the publish step has no arm. And two of the new arms pass on 0240's own base, so they are regression guards rather than arms that were red before the fix.

- **Done when 1.** releasepublish.bats: "a publishing project's dry-run cut plans its push to local alone, and its snapshot, candidate and publish rows wait on release publish (0240)", the confirm row naming no origin and the stand-in public repository unchanged; "a publishing project's cut pushes to local alone and stops after the push, and the stand-in public repository receives nothing (0240)", with a remote `public` at the stand-in repository that release.remotes leaves out, origin untouched, local holding the release commit and tag, and no "is released" line; and "a publishing cut refuses at pre-flight to push to a remote that names the publish repository, naming it, and writes nothing (0240)", with release.remotes undeclared, so a cut would push to every remote.
- **Done when 2.** "release publish pushes the snapshot, never a workroom commit, to candidate/<tag>, then on green moves main and pushes a lightweight tag, each read back, and deletes the candidate (0240)" holds the public main to the snapshot's identity and tree, the workroom's release commit absent, no object in the public repository the snapshot does not reach, and CI asked first about the snapshot with no tag while the candidate alone held it. "a red candidate moves neither main nor the tag, says why, and stays as the record of it (0240)", "a candidate run still going past ci.wait moves neither main nor the tag, and the same command run again reads CI again and publishes that candidate (0240)" and "a verdict that cannot be read, from a query that fails or one that answers no verdict, moves neither main nor the tag (0240)" hold each other verdict, and "--expect refuses a snapshot of any other sha, pushing nothing, and publishes the one release snapshot printed (0240)" holds `--expect`. The arms use the fixtures' stub ci.query (ci_query_decl, ci_answers), as releasecut.bats's do.
- **Done when 3.** "release publish refuses at pre-flight a remote that names the publish repository through an ssh host alias, naming it, reading nothing and writing nothing (0240)" (origin over https, publish.url `git@gh-alias:T/Demo.git`) and "release publish refuses at pre-flight a remote whose pushurl alone names the publish repository, naming it, and writes nothing (0240)" hold the url, the pushurl and the alias, and Done when 1's last arm holds the cut's own refusal. "a remote names the publish repository however its path is spelled, or as the same local path, and one whose url says too little to tell is refused as unknown (0240)" holds `release_remote_naming` to C1 and W1 in a table: a leading slash after an scp host and a doubled slash after an https host name t/pub (rc 0), a remote url naming a host and three path segments answers rc 2 naming it, and a path reached through `..` names the same local repository by `-ef`. The table holds the function's answer; each caller's refusal on rc 2 is in the code above.
- **Done when 4.** Each ref is read back in Done when 2's first arm. "a public tag already at another commit is refused before anything is pushed, and CI is not asked (0240)", "a candidate branch holding another commit is refused before anything is pushed (0240)", "a publish branch that moves while CI runs is never forced: the publish step stops and the tag is not pushed (0240)" and "a tag another hand pushes while CI runs is refused at the publish step, and main does not move (0240)" hold the refusals and that nothing is forced. W2 is held by "a public tag already at the snapshot does not stand for CI: with main still to move, a red candidate moves nothing (0240)" and "a resume with main moved and no tag pushed reads CI on the candidate again, then pushes the tag at the same snapshot (0240)". "a finished publish run again finds the snapshot published, asks nothing and pushes nothing (0240)", "a second release is made on the first: its snapshot's parent is the public tip, main fast-forwards, a re-run finds it, and the first release run again is refused as public already (0240)" and "release publish --dry-run makes the snapshot, asks nothing, and pushes nothing (0240)" hold the re-runs and the dry run.
- **Done when 5.** "under publish.url validation refuses ci.base, and publish.candidate needs publish.url and must hold the tag and more (0240)" refuses ci.base under publish.url, each bad candidate template, and publish.url with a release.verbs that leaves out publish, and accepts a publishing block whose ci.query has ci.tag off. ci-workflow.bats: "the workflow runs on a release tag, a candidate branch and on demand, as well as on a push to main (0108) (0240)", "the macOS job is gated on the ref TYPE, a candidate branch and on demand, never on a tag's form (0108) (0240)" and "a release's candidate runs the whole matrix: the push filter and the macOS, WSL and summary conditions name the branch release.publish.candidate's default makes (0240)". formula.bats: "under release.publish.url render takes the revision from the public repository's tag, which names the snapshot, never this checkout's commit (0240)", "under release.publish.url render refuses a tag the public repository does not carry yet, and writes nothing (0240)", "under release.publish.url an annotated public tag gives the commit it names, never the tag object, as the revision (0240)" and "devbin's template fetches the public repository over https, as anyone's brew can (0240)". ci-state.bats's "devbin publishes through CI on its candidate: publish.url the public repository, its cut to local alone, ci.base left out, ci.tag off, this query asked about release.repo (0240)" holds devbin's own config. A project without publish.url: "a project without publish.url cuts as before: the snapshot, candidate and publish rows skipped, the release pushed and made (0240)", "release status reads the snapshot, candidate and publish rows as skipped without publish.url (0240)" and "release publish in a project without publish.url is refused, naming the key (0240)", with "release status reads the snapshot, candidate and publish rows as not read, naming release publish, under publish.url (0240)" beside them, and releasecut.bats run whole in the light phase.
- **Done when 6.** lib/pages/release.md, lib/config.reference.yaml, docs/configuration.md and docs/releasing.md document the verb and its keys; "release publish's arguments are read before anything acts: one version, and --expect a whole sha, for release publish alone (0240)" reads its usage line, and releasecore.bats's arms tagged (0240) read the new verb, keys and readers. The landing suite: C's arms phase, in estate slot 01M61TNPWJTZMYNDBPTEZZ54ZG on molt-vc's grant, ran every arm tagged with one of the bank's eight issues on main 09c7d61a, file by file, from 2026-10-28 18:00Z to 18:08Z: in the red clone f4b30a50, main's lib with the bank's tests, under BSD; then at the bank's tip 53c92332 under BSD, and again with GNU coreutils, findutils, sed and grep first on PATH (~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/s5e/runs/arms/, summary in s5e/arms.out). Each of 0240's 40 arms failed in the red clone and passed under BSD and GNU. C was stopped on hv's word in its light phase, so its whole-file legs, the tree scans among them, did not finish; hv's runs on main took them over. hv's first test all on main (tmp/test/20261029-0614) found three breaches in 0240's code, which caf77878 fixed: contract.bats 338, where publish_run's git_local_env_clear failure exited 2 and now exits 3; helpers.bats 1177 (0066), where the publish refs now read an empty field as empty through dash_to_empty in lib/helpers and test with -n and -z, never against the - sentinel; and updatenotice.bats 2561 (0079), where publish now asks whether the tag is in the parent's history through commit_direction. The next test all (tmp/test/20261029-0727) failed releasepublish.bats 2035, 2037, 2039, 2045 and 2055, since the no-parent comparison still spelled none as -; 217adf65 reads both as empty. hv's `dvb test all` on rhadamanth at 217adf65 ran every one of the 2777 tests bats counts in tests/unit once, and none failed (tmp/test/20261029-0817.bats.out, its .errors empty). K0116B, the full suite on kovacs at 4d1a76b0 with rustup's cargo first on PATH, as on CI's Ubuntu runner, is green, as vc read its seal. CI run 40851772728 on 4d1a76b0 and CI run 40860048152 on 25175386, the head 0.1.16 was cut from, are green on Test on Ubuntu, Shell Script Analysis and Test Summary. No critic leg ran on the landed commits.

- **CI:** run 40860048152 on the pushed head 25175386, which carries the landing, read green by vc.
